adjudicated_non_defects.feature: The read-merge-write of ledger.json is performed by the model rather than by a shipped upsert script.
adjudicated_non_defects.why_it_looks_wrong: Read JSON, find the entry by tag, merge or append, write the whole file back is precisely specifiable, repeatable and mechanically checkable, so it reads as R11 deterministic work left to freeform generation.
adjudicated_non_defects.why_it_is_correct: R11 detects *repeated* mechanical work — repeated parsing, exact sorting, static inventory, deterministic shell loops. One read-merge-write per release is not a loop. R11's opposite failure direction governs instead: mandating scripts/upsert_release.py for a single-object JSON upsert buys a file, an interface and a dependency for low-risk work, which is over-extraction. A finding that cites R11 to require the script is a false positive.
adjudicated_non_defects.adjudicated: 2026-08-20, independent adjudication of the EX-015 dispute against R11. FALSE POSITIVE, High confidence.

adjudicated_non_defects.feature: The workflow gives no explicit branch for a ledger that already contains more than one entry for the tag.
adjudicated_non_defects.why_it_looks_wrong: 'Search the ledger for an entry whose tag equals this tag' assumes zero-or-one match, so a pre-duplicated ledger reads as undefined behaviour in a mutating Skill.
adjudicated_non_defects.why_it_is_correct: R19 scopes to duplication the Skill inflicts on itself — its Check is 'can rerunning a mutating Skill duplicate or corrupt state' and its Detect is executing the operation twice against controlled state. A duplicate present before the run can only come from another writer, and the Skill passes R19's own test: the tag is the entry identity and an existing entry is updated in place, never appended beside. The case is also already covered rather than undefined: Done-when requires exactly one entry for the tag, so a pre-duplicated ledger cannot be reported as done, and the failure section requires reporting with the ledger left as found. Adding an explicit branch restates a guard the fixture already carries.
adjudicated_non_defects.adjudicated: 2026-08-20, independent adjudication of the EX-015 dispute against R19. FALSE POSITIVE, High confidence.

controls_present.evidence: The tag is the entry identity; an existing entry is updated in place and a re-run is required to leave the file byte-identical apart from changed fields.
Three named failure modes with distinct handling; the retry is bounded at two attempts and only for the plausibly transient lock case; the deterministic failure is explicitly not retried.
Done-when is observable and checkable: file parses, exactly one entry for the tag, prior entries intact. Failure reporting is required not to imply the write happened.
One file written, one read-only command, no network or credentials, stated as a scoping instruction to the host rather than a promise of good behaviour.
The unparseable-ledger guard protects the one output whose corruption is costly, and nothing more.

notes: The positive control for mutating workflows. EX-006 shows the reviewer catches an unsafe mutation; this fixture shows it does not simply raise mutation findings unconditionally. Marking R17-R20 'not applicable' here is a failure — they apply and are satisfied. The adjudicated_non_defects are deliberately easy to criticise and adjudicated correct: a reviewer that raises either has produced a semantic false positive.
change_policy: Frozen for the validation cycle. A new evidence-backed finding is DISPUTED and goes to independent adjudication, recorded here with its evidence, before this fixture changes.

R15 on the same prose-only invariant: TRUE POSITIVE in reduced form, Low severity, Medium-High confidence — SKILL.md:21-23 requires a re-run to leave the ledger 'byte-identical apart from any field whose value genuinely changed', which is a stronger property than the observable completion condition at SKILL.md:57-58 verifies (parses, exactly one entry for the tag, prior entries still present — presence, not serialisation), and stronger than whole-file regeneration from the structure read at SKILL.md:33 can guarantee.
